name: Gulf / US–Iran war
value: Tankers hit; Trump says strikes unlikely
summary: Trump tells CNN renewed strikes are unlikely if talks progress; blasts at Qeshm and tanker fires reported on 8 Nov
state: President Trump told CNN on 8 Nov that renewed strikes were highly unlikely to be needed while nuclear and Hormuz talks progress, while saying bridges remained in US sights (Israel Hayom). Four explosions were heard at Bahman Port on Qeshm, cause unclear. CENTCOM said a US aircraft disabled a St Kitts-flagged ship in the Gulf of Oman on 7 Nov (ABC Australia). The Revolutionary Guards said three tankers caught fire, and UKMTO reported a tanker hit by a projectile (Iran International). Foreign Minister Araghchi said mediators had stopped travelling.
for_you: FCDO travel advice is the official guide for Iran and the Gulf states. Continued shipping attacks feed through to fuel and freight costs.
rubric_hit: Active US–Iran strikes and attacks on Gulf shipping = Alert

sources.title: Israel Hayom — Trump: renewed strikes on Iran highly unlikely

why: Direct hostilities between Iran and the US or Israel threaten Gulf energy infrastructure, the Strait of Hormuz and the wider region.
drivers: Strikes and retaliation, attacks on shipping and Gulf states, mediation and ceasefire talks, US force posture.

rubric.alert: Active strikes between states, attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure or shipping, or the Strait of Hormuz substantially closed.
rubric.watch: A ceasefire or stalemate with sporadic strikes, or credible threats of renewed strikes.
rubric.normal: No direct state-on-state hostilities; diplomacy active.
